per_window.ps-ns: dynamic_in_window at specific sites, measured only with Mg2+ or BeFx at 25 °C. Mg-bound unphosphorylated WT: lowest backbone S2 at K91 in the β4-α4 loop (CHEY-J12, r8), rigid remainder S2 0.66-0.94, mean 0.88 (CHEY-J13, no_evidence_in_window, r8), methyl S2axis 0.25-0.99 with flexible T87 Cγ2 and A90 Cβ (CHEY-J14, r9). BeFx-bound: active-site methyls rigidify, nearby methyls loosen, A90 stays flexible (CHEY-J15, r10, r11). Mg-free WT: not_measured (CHEY-J16). The urea-denatured F14N/V83T study (CHEY-J23, r37) is excluded from the native verdict.
per_window.us-ms: dynamic_in_window in every native state measured. Mg-free WT (1 mM EDTA, 15 °C): 13 residues with per-residue local-fit kex 96 ± 16 to 2,440 ± 570 s-1 and per-residue pI 0.67-0.99 (local fits, not a shared population; group fit failed) (CHEY-J1, r1); D13 broadened (CHEY-J2, r5); nothing above Rex 2 s-1 elsewhere (CHEY-J3). 10 mM Mg2+: 11 residues, per-residue kex 246 ± 31 to 3,620 ± 460 s-1, per-residue pI 0.91-0.99 (CHEY-J4, r2), a suspected second faster process at A88 (CHEY-J5), G39 broadened (CHEY-J6), nothing elsewhere by CPMG or model-free (CHEY-J7). Two-point Rex peaks at 1 mM Mg2+ and is lower at 75 mM, the latter from Figure 3 only (CHEY-J8, r3, r4). BeFx-activated CheY keeps small, redistributed exchange (CHEY-J9, r7). Moy 1994, abstract only, Mg present: exchange near the Mg-binding loop (CHEY-J10, r26). Parameter differences across Mg conditions are condition differences, not conflicts.
per_window.slower_than_ms: not_measured for Mg-free WT (CHEY-J17; HDX-MS searched with no relevant paper; the only time-resolved row, r18, is F14N refolding and is not judged).
per_window.undetermined: Structure-only: Mg-free WT crystals show correlated two-conformer β4-α4 loop and Y106 (CHEY-J18, r19, r27); FliM-peptide-bound Mg-CheY shows intermediate loop conformers (CHEY-J19, r12); the Mg-bound crystal rearrangement is unresolved against solution data (CHEY-J20, r21); BeF3-activated structure with α4 amide-exchange protection (CHEY-J21, r13). MD: 1 μs apo simulation (CHEY-J22, r39, md_only). CheA P1-CheY arrangement at 283 K and 303 K is binding kinetics, not counted (CHEY-J11, r16, r17). Not judged: r14, r33 (phospho/BeFx chemical-shift endpoints), r15 (CheA PRE docking), r18 (refolding intermediate), r20, r24 (BeF3/Mn and CheZ-peptide crystals, abstract only), r22 (Salmonella homolog), r23, r30, r31, r32 (phosphorylation and signalling kinetics), r25, r38 (MD with mutant, peptide or BeF3-removed starts), r28 (in-cell resting state), r29 (T87I crystal, abstract only, no motion measured), r34 (in-cell intermolecular FRET), r35, r36 (activating mutant crystal and 19F), r40, r41 (Thermotoga homolog EPR), r42, r43 (XFMS accessibility of FliM-bound CheY).

protein_summary.wt_apo_answer: Yes: at 15 °C without Mg2+ (50 mM sodium phosphate pH 7.0, 1 mM EDTA), unphosphorylated wild-type CheY shows microsecond-millisecond exchange at 13 active-site and FliM-face residues (R18, R19, A36, D38, N62, D64, E67, L68, L69, T87, N94, V107, L127, plus broadened D13); per-residue local two-state fits give kex from 96 ± 16 s-1 (D64) to 2,440 ± 570 s-1 (V107) and per-residue major fractions pI 0.99 to 0.67, which are local fit parameters, not a shared population; no global rate or population exists because group fitting failed, and no phosphate-free control was run.
open_conflicts: Exchange model for the same CPMG data (r1, r2): the authors' per-residue local fits, failed group fits and poor Δω-Δδ correlation argue against a concerted two-state inactive-active switch, while the linear chemical-shift trajectories of E89, Y106 and V107 (and nearly M85, A97, A98) across T87I, WT, A113P and BeFx states fit a classic two-state equilibrium shift; the authors reconcile them as segmental local switching.

Two-state versus three-state at 10 mM Mg2+ (r2 source text): an F-test favours a three-state model for A36, T87 and E89, but the three-state fits were not robust and group three-state fitting gave no improvement; in EDTA no residue improved.

Mg2+ effect on structure: the Mg-bound E. coli crystal shows displacements up to 10 Å at the α4 N terminus and preceding loop (r21), while McDonald 2012 solution chemical-shift perturbations on Mg2+ addition are small in the allosteric region (cited in r1/r2 paper).
Residual exchange in BeFx-activated CheY (r7): authors leave open whether it is local return to the inactive state, motion among several active-like states, or motions slowed into the CPMG window.
questions_for_gina: The RelaxDB source lead names Table 2 (Rex labels) and Figure 2 (missing-peak labels), i.e. the Mg-free 1 mM EDTA sample; the text names only D13 as too broad there, and Figure 2A marks too-broad residues only in the image. Which residues carry the missing-peak label, and should the 10 mM Mg2+ Table 1 set be kept out of the labels?

All CPMG and relaxation samples used 50 mM sodium phosphate pH 7.0 with no phosphate-free control, and the Mg-free crystal 3CHY has a sulfate next to N59/K109 in the phosphorylation pocket; do you know of a buffer comparison for CheY, or should the active-site exchange (D13, D38, N62, D64) be flagged as untested for anion binding?
protein_summary.buffer_note: Untested condition, not a demonstrated artefact: every native CheY NMR dynamics sample in the rows (McDonald 2012, r1-r6; McDonald 2013, r7-r11) was in 50 mM sodium phosphate, 0.02% NaN3, pH 7.0, and no source reports a phosphate-free control, although CheY is phosphorylated at D57 and binds phosphoryl analogues there; the Mg2+ Kd of 1.5 mM was also measured in this buffer. The Mg-free apo crystal 3CHY contains three sulfate ions (verified in the cached mmCIF ~/dynamics_atlas_work/structures/CHEY_CPMG/cif/3CHY.cif.gz); by a 4.5 Å contact check run here, one sits next to N59 and K109 in the phosphorylation pocket, one near G105, Y106, K119 and K122, and one near G76. The Mg-free sample contains 1 mM EDTA and the Mg-bound sample 10 mM MgCl2 (about 86% occupied); they give different per-residue parameters and are separate states. CPMG samples were >80% deuterated, 2H-relaxation samples about 60%. All CPMG pI values are per-residue local fits, not populations. The denatured-state study used 25 mM sodium phosphate with 5 M urea (r37).

judgments.function_link: Authors propose these asynchronous local motions are the basis of CheY allostery (segmental switching between inactive and active-like conformations), not a concerted two-state switch.

detection.detection_window: 15N relaxation-compensated CPMG at 600 and 700 MHz, 15 °C; 12 or 13 τcp values with duplicates, 40 ms total CPMG period (one data set used 20 ms). The text gives the τcp extremes only through the two-point Rex screen, which used τcp 10.0 and 0.556 ms as the lowest and highest τcp of the dispersion set. A residue counted only with Rex > 2 s-1 and an F-test (α 0.01) favouring exchange. Misses exchange with Rex below 2 s-1 (small Δω or minor population), exchange faster than about 3,000-5,000 s-1 (authors' usable range a few hundred to about 3,000 s-1), and amides that are unassigned, overlapped, broadened out or prolines.

judgments.reason: Outside the 13 fitted residues and D13, the Mg-free CPMG data show no exchange above the 2 s-1 threshold, which limits detectable exchange to the active-site and FliM face but does not exclude smaller or faster motions elsewhere.
